about: Why boredom is good for children

lines.text: Parents today go to great lengths to make sure their children are never bored.
Weekends are filled by tuition, music lessons and sports, leaving hardly a free hour.
lines.note: Preposition: a day is 'filled with' activities.

lines.text: Psychologists, however, have begun to argue that boredom was useful. A child
lines.note: Tense: this is a general claim, so it is 'is useful'.

lines.text: with nothing to do is forced to invention a game, tell a story
lines.note: Word form: after 'to' a verb is needed — 'invent'.

lines.text: or simply think. These are the moments in which imagination grows. In one
study, adults who were given a dull task first later produced more original ideas
as those who were not. Boredom also teaches patience, because a child who
is entertain every minute never learns to wait. Lessons and sports are not
harmful, so a timetable still needs some empty space in it. The next
lines.note: Connector: the second idea limits the first — a contrast, 'but'.

lines.text: time a child complains for having nothing to do, a wise parent might
resist the urge to help. The complain usually lasts ten minutes; the game
lines.note: Word form: after 'the' a noun is needed — 'complaint'.

lines.text: that follows it can last the whole afternoon.
